result.question: I'm worried the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at MAIN may be involved. Pull co and co2 for every sample in the available window and work out the CO2/CO ratio for each sample. Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. If co2 has no data at all, report the co trend alongside oxygen instead and say that the ratio test couldn't be done.
result.answer:
**Transformer 1 at MAIN: CO₂/CO ratio check**

All 5 samples (15–19 Jan 2024) have both CO and CO₂ readings, so I calculated the ratio for every sample.

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO₂ (ppm) | CO₂/CO | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.00 | Above 10 (general cellulose ageing) |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.33 | Above 10 (general cellulose ageing) |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.57 | Above 10 (general cellulose ageing) |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.15 | Above 10 (general cellulose ageing) |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.88 | Above 10 (general cellulose ageing) |

**Summary statistics over the window**
- **CO:** min 30, max 35, mean 32.4 ppm
- **CO₂:** min 1300, max 1350, mean 1331.8 ppm

**Trend:** The ratio is drifting down slightly, but it's close to flat. The line of best fit falls by about 0.34 per sample. The values rose to 43.33 on 16 Jan, dropped to 38.57 on 17 Jan, then climbed back to 41.88, close to where they started (42.00). That's more like normal sample-to-sample variation than a real trend.

**What this means:** No sample is below 3, so there's no sign that paper is involved in an active fault. Every sample is well above 10, at about 39–43, which points to slow general ageing of the paper insulation rather than a fault. Five daily samples is a short window, so it would be worth keeping an eye on the ratio over a longer period.
